note: βασιλεύων ἄνθρωπον ὑποκριτὴν takes an object: he makes a hypocrite king; “reigning” lost the object.
δυσκολίας λαοῦ: the genitive needs “of”, the perverseness of the people.
ἐνεχυράσω is a first-person future: I will take as pledge; “you took” gave the wrong person and tense.
συνετοὶ καρδίας: καρδίας is a genitive singular, discerning of heart; “hearts” made it a plural noun with no case.
ἐναντίον τοῦ Κυρίου: the preposition gives “before” and τοῦ “the”; “of the Lord” doubled them.
ἑαυτῶν follows the first-person ἑλώμεθα and γνῶμεν: among ourselves, not “their own”.
ἐπισκοπὴ ἀνδρὸς: the genitive is the man who is looked after, oversight of a man.
ἐπισκοπὴ αὐτῷ: the dative gives for whom the care is.
ἕκαστος αὐτῶν is partitive: each of them.
τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ ποιῶν: τίς is “who”; “what kind” is ποῖος.
AD ἀπ᾿ with the accusative ἄνδρα is a misprint for ἐπ᾿, as Athens prints: he will not set it upon a man.
δὲ joins the second clause here; the alternative gloss is resolved to “and”.
δεῖξόν μοι: the dative is the one shown, show to me.
ἀπὸ ὕβρεως πονηρῶν is causal, because of the insolence of the wicked; “before” is not the sense.
ὥς ἐστι is a comparison, as he is; “so as” suggests purpose.
ἡγήσω is aorist: what did you reckon this; the future was wrong.
σὺ τίς εἶ ὅτι εἶπας: ὅτι is consecutive, who are you that you said; it is not causal.
καὶ τοῖς τρισὶ φίλοις σου: the dative is the second recipient of the answer, to the three friends.
ὡς ὑψηλὰ ἀπὸ σοῦ: ὑψηλὰ is a predicate adjective, how high they are; “high places” made it a noun.

grammar: aorist active indicative, second singular, in a rhetorical question
note: εἰ ἥμαρτες is a conditional, if you sinned; “have you sinned” made it a question.
τί πράξεις is a future verb, what will you do; “deeds” read it as a noun.
λήψεται ἐκ χειρός σου is to receive from your hand; “seize” adds force the Greek lacks.
εἰ δὲ καὶ: δὲ is glossed “and”, so καὶ is adverbial “even”; “and and” doubled it.
